name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's 25-point Republican partisan lean in an open-seat race
Polymarket prices the Republican at 97 percent
Tom Sell's $2.5 million raised and $1.3 million in outside support versus $49,000 for Kyle Rable
No public polling or expert ratings indicate competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's 25-point Republican lean, a 97 percent Republican price on Polymarket, and a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage for Tom Sell all point to a safe Republican hold despite the open seat created by Jodey Arrington's retirement.
model.watch: A major candidate scandal, a late wave of Democratic outside spending, or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race could move the outlook, though no such evidence currently exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 19th District is an open seat after Republican Jodey Arrington announced his retirement, but little else about the race appears open. The district leans Republican by roughly 25 points, and no general-election polling exists to suggest a competitive contest. Prediction markets on Polymarket price the Republican nominee at about 97 percent, effectively treating the seat as decided.

Financial figures point the same direction. Republican Tom Sell has raised about $2.5 million, supplemented by roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $49,000 with minimal cash on hand. With a favorable district, a large money advantage, and market pricing all aligned, the seat is rated Safe Republican, with the main question being the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
